name: Hexarelin (Examorelin)
lead: Hexarelin (also called examorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP) that stimulates growth hormone (GH) release by activating the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, the receptor for the gut hormone ghrelin. [1][2][3] Reviews describe it as more chemically stable and more potent than ghrelin itself. [3]

It has been studied in clinical endocrinology since the mid-1990s, including in healthy volunteers, people with GH deficiency and elderly adults. [4][5][6] It is not an approved medicine. In bodybuilding forums it is discussed as a potent, cheaper GHRP, often paired with a GHRH analogue. [7][8][9]

Published human studies have measured hormone responses, not muscle, fat or appearance outcomes. A 16-week study in healthy elderly people was designed to test whether the GH response weakens with long-term use, a limitation that the investigators described as potentially serious for therapeutic use. [10]

paras: Hexarelin is one of several GHRPs, together with GHRP-1, GHRP-2 and GHRP-6, that were synthesised to release GH in animals and humans; reviews note these peptides are structurally unrelated to GHRH and act on receptors at the pituitary or hypothalamus. [1][11]

Beyond the pituitary, hexarelin binds peripheral receptors. A review of its cardiovascular action reports that the scavenger receptor CD36 serves as a cardiac receptor mediating cardioprotective effects, and another review describes a GHRP-CD36-PPARγ pathway that links hexarelin to lipid metabolism, atherosclerosis and fat mitochondrial biogenesis in preclinical work. [3][12]

Studies in humans have also shown endocrine effects other than GH: hexarelin stimulated the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis via arginine vasopressin, stimulated prolactin in acromegalic but not hyperprolactinaemic patients, and had no effect on TRH-induced TSH response. [13][14][15]

Controlled human studies of hexarelin date mostly from the 1990s and concern endocrine physiology. A randomised comparison found that hexarelin-induced GH release was influenced by exogenous GH, and a trial in GH-deficient patients examined its effect on GH secretion. [4][5] Others described effects on cortisol, prolactin and TSH. [13][14][15]

In 12 healthy elderly participants given twice-daily injections for 16 weeks, investigators examined whether the GH response became attenuated, framing such desensitization as a potential limit on therapeutic use. [10] A review on GH in obesity notes that GHRP-6 and hexarelin evoke larger GH responses in obese patients than GHRH, but smaller than in lean subjects. [16]

A human study comparing ghrelin and hexarelin found that both affected glucose and insulin levels. [17] No studies found of hexarelin for muscle gain, fat loss or physical appearance in healthy people.

sections.h: Use in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing communities
paras: On T Nation, hexarelin appears in lists of peptides some users report having tried, sometimes as an alternative to ipamorelin, and sometimes with HCG, SARMs and anti-oestrogens. [7][18][19] One poster cites a YouTube creator who says hexarelin outperforms other GH peptides; another notes GHRP-6 plus hexarelin can be found cheaply. [18][20]
Posters repeat a claim that giving GHRH together with GHRP-6, GHRP-2 or hexarelin leads to synergistic GH release. [8][21]

Analytical chemistry research has looked at detecting related GHRP compounds, including a 2025 study identifying consumption biomarkers for alexamorelin, a related compound, in human hepatocyte incubations. [22]

timeline.event: Clinical trials report hexarelin effects on GH release in healthy and GH-deficient people. [4][5]
A study tests whether hexarelin's GH response weakens over 16 weeks in healthy elderly adults. [10]
Studies compare hexarelin with ghrelin and GHRH in humans. [17][23]

lore.intro: Hexarelin is described on T Nation as a strong GHRP, used by some in peptide stacks for GH release. [7][18]

claims.claim: Hexarelin is the most potent GH peptide
claims.believers: A poster relays a YouTube creator's view that hexarelin outperforms other GH peptides and chooses it over ipamorelin. [18]
claims.experts: Reviews describe it as potent in releasing GH, but no cited study compares muscle or appearance outcomes between peptides. [1][3]

claims.claim: GHRP plus GHRH gives synergistic GH release
claims.believers: Posters state that GHRH given with GHRP-6, GHRP-2 or hexarelin produces a synergistic release of GH. [8][21]
claims.experts: Reviews describe GHRP and GHRH acting at distinct receptors; combined GHRH plus GHRP-6 is described as the most powerful GH-releasing stimulus in obesity. [1][16]

claims.claim: Hexarelin builds muscle without water retention
claims.believers: A user reports solid gains without water retention after using GHRPs, including hexarelin. [7]
claims.experts: No study cited tests hexarelin for muscle gain in healthy people.

card.summary: A potent GH-releasing peptide studied in 1990s endocrine trials; forum favourite, no evidence for looks, with desensitization questions.
card.note: Also hits cortisol and prolactin axes; GH response may fade.

quick.overview:
Hexarelin is a lab-made peptide that mimics ghrelin to force a big growth hormone release. Forum users pick it as a strong, cheap GH peptide for muscle and recovery.

Human trials measured hormone levels only; none tested muscle, fat or appearance.
quick.mechanism: It activates the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor, and also CD36 in the heart, driving GH release and effects on other hormones.
quick.risks: It also raises cortisol and prolactin in some studies, and a 16-week trial was built to test whether the GH response fades. It is not approved as a medicine.
